n: Micah addresses Israel’s rulers. Shouldn’t they, of all people, know what justice is? Leaders are responsible for fairness.
Instead they hate good and love evil. Micah uses a shocking image: they skin the people alive.

f.w: Who hate the good, and love the evil

n: Like butchers, they chop up God’s people and cook them in a pot. The image shows how they consume the poor for their own gain.

f.w: eat the flesh of my people

n: When disaster comes, they’ll cry to the Lord, but He won’t answer. Those who ignore the cries of the poor will find their own cries unheard.
False prophets mislead the people. They preach “peace” to anyone who feeds them, and declare war on anyone who doesn’t.

f.g: Have something to chew on — when they are fed.

n: Their spiritual light will go out. Night will fall on them; they’ll receive no visions or answers.

f.g: Practice divination — seek hidden knowledge by occult means.

f.w: the sun shall go down over the prophets

n: These seers and diviners will be humiliated and cover their mouths like mourners, because God gives them no answer.

f.g: A gesture of shame or mourning (Leviticus 13:45).

n: In contrast, Micah is filled with power from the Lord’s Spirit, with justice and courage to name Israel’s sin. True prophets speak by the Spirit, whether popular or not.

f.w: I am full of power by the spirit of the LORD

n: Micah again calls out the leaders who despise justice and twist what is right.

f.g: Make crooked everything that is straight.

n: They build Jerusalem’s grand buildings with blood and injustice — through forced labor and exploitation.
Judges take bribes, priests teach for pay, and prophets tell fortunes for money — yet they claim, “The Lord is with us; nothing bad can happen.” Religion has become a business.

f.w: the priests thereof teach for hire
Is not the LORD among us?

n: Because of these leaders, Zion will be plowed like a field and the temple hill overgrown like a forest. A century later, elders saved Jeremiah’s life by recalling this prophecy and how Hezekiah repented.

f.w: Zion for your sake be plowed as a field
